title: Frontend: Sliding Window Maximum
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Sliding Window Maximum. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({values,k}). Return maximum values for each window of positive integer size k <= values.length, using a monotonic index deque. Invalid k throws Invalid window.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Maintain a deque of candidate indices in decreasing value order.
alternativeApproaches: Return maximum positions with a documented oldest-versus-newest tie policy for equal values.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: k=1; k=n; duplicates.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
